g.text: Critical vs Stationary Points, 1st/2nd/Higher Derivative Tests, Points of Inflection, and Global Extrema Protocol
Critical Points vs Stationary Points Distinction
f'(x₀) = 0 OR f'(x₀) does NOT exist
Broad superset including corners, cusps & horizontal tangents.
Tangent is strictly horizontal (zero slope). Every stat point is critical.
If f(x) has a local extremum at x = c and f is differentiable at c, then f'(c) MUST EQUAL 0.
• Could be Max, Min or Inflection
Let f'(c) = f''(c) = ... = f^{(n-1)}(c) = 0, and f^{(n)}(c) ≠ 0 (First non-vanishing derivative):
Case A: Order n is ODD
x = c is a POINT OF INFLECTION
• Neither a local maximum nor minimum!
• Canonical Example: f(x) = x³ at x = 0
Case B: Order n is EVEN
x = c is a LOCAL EXTREMUM
Even-order curvature acts identical to 2nd derivative.
• Tangent lines lie BELOW the curve.
• First derivative f'(x) is monotonically increasing.
• Tangent lines lie ABOVE the curve.
• First derivative f'(x) is monotonically decreasing.
A point (c, f(c)) is a Point of Inflection IF AND ONLY IF:
CRITICAL TRAP: f''(c) = 0 is NOT sufficient! For f(x) = x⁴, f''(0) = 0, but f''(x) = 12x² ≥ 0 never changes sign. x = 0 is a MINIMUM, NOT an inflection point!
4. GLOBAL EXTREMA ON CLOSED INTERVALS [a, b]
Step 1: Find all critical points in open interval (a, b)
Solve f'(x) = 0 and locate points where f'(x) does not exist: c₁, c₂, ..., cₖ ∈ (a, b).
Step 2: Evaluate f(x) at all interior critical points
Step 3: Evaluate f(x) at BOTH boundary endpoints
Calculate values: f(a) and f(b). NEVER SKIP BOUNDARIES!
GLOBAL MAXIMUM = max { f(a), f(b), f(c₁), f(c₂), ... }
GLOBAL MINIMUM = min { f(a), f(b), f(c₁), f(c₂), ... }
For f(x) = A cos x + B sin x : Range = [-√(A² + B²), +√(A² + B²)]
• Maximum occurs at: tan x = B / A (in quadrant matching signs)
• GATE Trap: If interval is restricted (e.g. [0, π/2]), boundary evaluation is mandatory!
• Domain: Exclude division by zero, negative radicands, log(≤0).
• Intercepts: y-intercept = f(0); x-intercepts = roots of f(x) = 0.
• Even f(-x) = f(x) ⟹ Symmetric about y-axis (sketch x ≥ 0 then reflect).
• Odd f(-x) = -f(x) ⟹ Symmetric about origin (180° rotation).
• Vertical: Points x = a where lim_{x➔a} f(x) = ±∞.
• Horizontal: Lines y = L where lim_{x➔±∞} f(x) = L.
• Slant / Oblique: y = mx + c when degree(Num) = degree(Denom) + 1.
• Compute f'(x), find all zeros and undefined points.
• Construct sign chart for f'(x): intervals of increase (+) and decrease (-).
• Classify local extrema via first derivative test.
• Compute f''(x), find zeros and sign change points.
• Intervals of concave up (f'' > 0) and concave down (f'' < 0).
• Mark inflection points where curvature flips.
Step 6: Master Worked Example • f(x) = x³ - 3x
• f''(x) = 6x ⟹ Inflection point at x = 0 (f'' flips sign from - to +).
• Local Max: (-1, 2) since f''(-1) = -6 < 0. Local Min: (1, -2) since f''(1) = 6 > 0.
